resources.string: What YT does differently and how to use it
Settings → Player → Floating player with sound wave
Settings → General → Local Return YouTube Dislike extractor
Videos play without ad clips or ad banners.
Subscriptions, playlists, Watch later and history work without signing in. If you like, sign in to YouTube and take your data over.
The feed is put together on your phone, and your subscriptions and history are kept there. YouTube personalises nothing.
“Play in background” in a video’s menu plays only the sound, also with the screen locked and on through the queue.
When you leave the app, the video keeps playing in a small window: Android’s picture in picture or YT’s floating player (see Mini player).
Download videos and audio and play them without a connection.
Skips sponsors, self-promotion and other segments the community marked; set per category.
Replaces sensational titles and thumbnails with calmer ones from the community.
A small green-red bar at the like button shows the ratio. The numbers are estimates from Return YouTube Dislike.
Most of this exists in every design except Standard.
“What are you in the mood for?”
When you open the app, pick learning, music, your subscriptions or browsing; the home follows. A chip on the home changes the choice.
Set sources, length, freshness, variety, channels, words and topics, with a preview and “Why am I seeing this?”. Everything runs on your phone.
Puts together videos that fit your time and stops at a sensible point, such as the end of a chapter. The mini player shows the time left.
Left hides a video for 90 days (with “Undo”), right adds it to the end of the queue. Sensitivity can be set and calibrated.
Pause a channel for a week
Hides a channel on the homes for 7 days without blocking it: from the undo pill, the hold menu or the feed controls.
Drag a card onto the mini player
Hold a card and drag it onto the mini player: it plays next, or goes to the end if something is already waiting.
Drag the magnifier onto a card
Hold the search icon and drag it onto a card: searches for that video’s channel.
A long press on a card opens a menu: save, share, channel, add to the end, hide, pause channel, why am I seeing this.
Started videos get a thin progress bar, watched ones are dimmed with a “Watched” badge. To hide them altogether: feed controls → Watched videos.
All-caps titles appear in normal case, “!!!” becomes “!”, chains of emoji become one. Only the display changes.
Search in the style of the design
Opens above the screen with your history, suggestions and filters. Switched off (and in Standard) you get the field in the top bar.
Search results show the same marks as the cards: progress bar, dimmed with a badge when watched.
Search field turns into a button
In Glass, Frost and Shapes the page’s search field turns smoothly into the button at the top as you scroll.
Hold the video: it shrinks under your finger and four tiles show your actions; drag to one and let go. 26 actions, set per direction.
While seeking, move your finger up: ½×, ¼×, ⅛×, then single frames. Optionally the video shows the spot live.
After a jump back, a chip takes you back to where you were.
Repeat a section A–B, if you like slower and with a pause to think. Long press on the time bar, or use the player menu.
Once switched on, a double tap on the right jumps to the next chapter, on the left to the start of the chapter. Without chapters it seeks as usual.
Hold Share and drag onto the time bar: you pick the exact moment in the same movement.
Hold the like button: two tiles for Like and Dislike. Drag to Dislike and wait a moment to see the estimated count. Without a YouTube sign-in the rating stays on the phone.
“No spoilers” blurs comments about later moments; “This scene” shows only comments about the current part.
In the speed menu, “Remember for this channel” applies the speed to every video of that channel.
Drag the video down and it shrinks under your finger into the mini player. Drag up to open it, drag the mini player down to close it.
Hold the mini player: it grows a little and shows the next video; let go on it to play it.
Up to 10 minutes after swiping it away, hold “Subscriptions” in the bottom bar: the video comes back at the same spot with its queue (not yet in After).
A mini player you swiped away stays paused and silent for 60 seconds; bring it back in that time and it continues without reloading.
When you leave the app, the video plays on in YT’s own window with a wave that moves with the sound. Needs “Display over other apps”; switched off, YT uses Android’s picture in picture.
Every video continues where you stopped, in every player: saved every 5 seconds and on pause or switching. Finished videos start at 0 again.
“Play next” and “Add to the end” build a queue that stays when you tap other videos.
Plays only the sound, also on through the queue; for downloads without their own audio track, the sound of the video file.
Brings videos to a similar loudness, lifts quiet parts gently and keeps anything from clipping.
In the background, music videos load only the sound, and music starts from the beginning instead of the remembered spot (a link with a time still jumps there).
Below the threshold (20 % by default) without a charger, or in battery saver, YT plays at most 480p and 30 fps; full quality again from 5 % above it.
At 20, 15, 10 and 5 % a coloured edge around the video (green to red) and a short vibration show the level. “Preview” lets you try it.
Build, device, network, last update and last crash as text to copy, without account or token data.
After a crash, YT asks once on the next start whether you want to copy or share the report. Reports stay on the device.
Shows what takes space and clears thumbnails, caches and old update files. Subscriptions, history, settings and sign-in always stay.
YT downloads updates in the app, checks them and first shows what is new, fixed and changed since your version.
